clips.title: The story
paras: Beneath Moonbrook, the Deadmines hide the Defias Brotherhood's staging ground. Once a source of Stormwind's gold, the tunnels were abandoned in the First War and long feared as haunted. Edwin VanCleef and goblin engineers work there beyond the realm's eyes, building an engine of vengeance against the kingdom.

Before the First War, the Deadmines were called the greatest gold-producing center in human lands. Their gold supplied a third of Stormwind's reserves. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to darkness. Sir Anduin Lothar spent twenty months imprisoned by subterranean ogres while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity. Warchief Blackhand's rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages with the ogre Turok, and both met their ends there. Believed cursed and home only to shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.

After the Stonemasons' Guild was cast out of Stormwind without payment for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef reorganized the disenfranchised artisans into the Defias Brotherhood. Seeking a secure headquarters beyond the reach of Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia, the Brotherhood chose its central redoubt in the abandoned tunnels. They drove out the legitimate Miners' League, leaving Foreman Thistlenettle's doomed workers to perish and rise as undead ghouls. The shafts became an industrial war camp, guarded by lumbering ogres, seasoned brigands, and mechanical constructs. Picks, fires, and illicit industry echo through the lower mines once more.
